### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **44** documentable anchor(s).

**12** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 41 pages)`, `organization_id (literal, 35 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **144** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7c2eab929c6b724672849c5b295fa5e2f35d04c0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `78ccb8e203143571a69c68b0988aecd3e33bd9a6` — the merge of head `236d39daf47ce4b06c9e8757ccbe695af1ca1e19` into base `7c2eab929c6b724672849c5b295fa5e2f35d04c0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 78ccb8e203143571a69c68b0988aecd3e33bd9a6 && git checkout 78ccb8e203143571a69c68b0988aecd3e33bd9a6
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7c2eab929c6b724672849c5b295fa5e2f35d04c0 236d39daf47ce4b06c9e8757ccbe695af1ca1e19 && git checkout -B drift-repro 7c2eab929c6b724672849c5b295fa5e2f35d04c0 && git merge --no-ff 236d39daf47ce4b06c9e8757ccbe695af1ca1e19

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7c2eab929c6b724672849c5b295fa5e2f35d04c0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7c2eab929c6b724672849c5b295fa5e2f35d04c0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `357025dc9728e877d0c1c8acc3ef2c49058c9c73`
Local-runs: none

Read-only review of PR #24828 (18.x step 7, part 7a-3 of #24583): diff `ddb3360a4..357025dc9`, 15 files, +671/-970, read in a detached worktree; the card's report 6286869893, claim 6285134534, execution record 6285122667 and ruling A 6278609968; objectui at the pinned `.objectui-sha` (12dc7b4) and at its `origin/main`. Head check-runs at review time: every completed run is `success` or `skipped` (Build Core, Build Docs, Type Check x4, Lint x8, Check Changeset, PR Size, Governed Surface Queue Guard, the claim/single-writer guards, Dogfood Regression Gate); `Test Core (1/6)` through `(6/6)` were still `in_progress`. This PASS does not stand in for their green: a red shard is blocking under AGENTS.md's queue rule, and the merge-base is unchanged (`origin/main` = `ddb3360a4`).

### ① Derived judgments

**1. The shape (D2, ruling A) — holds.**
- `projectDeclaredRule` (`sharing-rule-service.ts:204-208`) spreads `{ deploymentWide: true }` for `DEPLOYMENT_WIDE_SCOPE` and `{ organization_id: scope }` otherwise, so a `single` projection carries the marker and no `organization_id` key, and a walled projection carries its organization and no marker (pinned at `sharing-rule.test.ts:1881-1885` and `:1991-1994`). The scope list is a `unique symbol` (`:154`), translated from the plugin's `[null]` at exactly one door, `setDeclaredRuleScopes` (`:537-539`); `addDeclaredRuleScope` (`:558-563`) refuses to add an organization beside the deployment scope. The switch stays the deployment-level activation-ledger row (`readSwitchedOffDeclaredRules`, applied before projection at `:943-945`). That is ruling A's shape for declared webhooks (`plugin-webhooks/src/auto-enqueuer.ts:170,583`): one declaration, one deployment-level switch, each grant stamped with its record's organization.
- **Forgery through a stored row: not possible.** `isDeploymentWideSharingRule` (`:176-178`) requires `deploymentWide === true` AND `isDeclaredSharingRule` (`managed_by === 'package' && id === name`, `:228-230`). Every stored row enters the service through `rowFromRule` (`:125-146`), which copies a fixed field list and never the marker — all seven stored-row materialisations use it (`:804, :808, :827, :853, :908, :1119, :1121`); the two remaining `sys_sharing_rule` reads (`:948` holders, `:1271` orphan sweep) project `name`/`organization_id`/`id` only. `defineRule` writes a fixed column list (`:836-852`), spreads no input, and `sys-sharing-rule.object.ts` declares no `deploymentWide` column. The only public method taking a rule object, `reconcileRuleForUser`, is fed from `service.listRules` (`recipient-membership-recompute.ts:270-281`), not from a caller-supplied row. No REST door accepts a rule body for evaluation.

**2. `criteriaContext`, no NULL branch — holds.**
- `criteriaContext` (`:1778-1783`): a non-empty string organization → `{ ...SYSTEM_CTX, tenantId }`; else the marker or a lean composition → `SYSTEM_CTX`; else `null`. `sweepContextOrReport` (`:1802-1818`) logs once per rule at `error` (fallback `warn`) with the ceremony remedy and is applied on all three doors: the whole-rule sweep (`findMatchingRows :1836-1837` → `[]`), the per-record hook (`matchRecord :1864-1865` → `null`) and the grant write itself (`grantOne :2289-2290` → `false`), so no caller can write a grant around the sweep. Pinned with a real `SqlDriver` at `rule-criteria-org-scope.test.ts:376-394` (matched 0, granted 0, exactly one error line across two evaluations) and `:459-471` (per-record). Note the consequence the log line does not state: an empty desired set makes `reconcile` revoke what that row had materialised earlier — the fail-closed direction, and the stated remedy still applies.
- Under `single` a deployment-wide projection runs under `SYSTEM_CTX` with no `tenantId`, which is the predicate D8 computes under `single` (none); grants are stamped by `SharingService.resolveSystemGrantOrganization` from the record (`sharing-service.ts:1604-1609`, threaded organization first, record second). Pinned: `rule-criteria-org-scope.test.ts:340-355` (`deal_a1→ORG_A`, `deal_b1/b2→ORG_B`).
- Under a wall each projection carries its organization as a string, so the sweep threads `tenantId = organization` through the driver's chokepoint and matches no other organization's rows; recipients expand through `TeamGraphService`/`BusinessUnitGraphService`/`PositionGraphService` built with `rule.organization_id` (`:2037-2081`); the grant context carries the same organization (`activeOrganizationId(context)` wins at `sharing-service.ts:1604`). Pinned at `rule-criteria-org-scope.test.ts:357-374` (`isolated`, two organizations, three grants, each in its own organization) and `sharing-rule.test.ts:1988-1998`. A literal `user` recipient (`:2041`) is returned unscreened — unchanged by this PR and pre-existing for stored rules; the grant row is stamped with the record's organization, so it is readable only inside that wall. One caveat, named in the report and not this PR's: until 7a-1 lands, `SqlDriver.applyTenantScope` still carries `OR organization_id IS NULL`, so a walled projection can match an organization-less RECORD (never another organization's); the test removes `deal_p1` for that reason (`:362-363`).

**3. The lean-embedding key — robust, not a leak.**
- `organizationsComposed` (`:1792-1795`) = `typeof engine.getSchema === 'function' ? !!engine.getSchema('sys_organization') : true`. The engine handed in is the real `IObjectQLEngine` (`sharing-plugin.ts:661,772-773`), whose `getSchema` is `this._registry.getObject(objectName)` (`engine.ts:11458-11460`) — the same fact the engine's own D9 stamper reads as `organizationObjectRegistered` (`engine.ts:7420-7424`). `sys_organization` is declared by `platform-objects/src/identity/sys-organization.object.ts` and registered in every standard boot; a walled boot cannot run without it (`resolveDeclaredRuleScopes` enumerates it, `sharing-plugin.ts:105`; R4 measured). An engine that cannot answer reads as composed, i.e. refuses. The lean branch is reachable only by a STORED row with no string organization — a walled declared projection never reaches it. Pinned both ways: lean CONTROL (`rule-criteria-org-scope.test.ts:396-418`, no `sys_organization`, sweeps 4, no error) against the organizations case (`:376-394`). No path by which a walled deployment evaluates it as `true`.

**4. Readers — hold.**
- `adminOrgScope` (`:888-892`) and `findRuleRowByName` (`:1145-1153`) are strict own-organization; system context / platform operator keep the unfiltered read asserted upstream by `assertCanManageRules`. `deleteRule` (`:1156-1200`) resolves through the same `findRuleRow`: an organization-bound admin can no longer reach an organization-less row at all (silent no-op, as for any row the caller cannot see; a declared name → 403 at `:1163-1170`), and system/platform callers are exactly the callers the deleted guard returned early for (`row.organization_id != null → return; isSystem → return; hasPlatformAuthority → return`). No admin, Setup or API path needs `assertCanDeletePlatformGlobalRule`: the row class it gated is unreachable by the only caller it refused. `hasPlatformAuthority` keeps its one live caller (`:718`). Setup's delete of a declared rule stays 403 (`sharing-rule.test.ts:1967`).
- `ApprovalService.businessUnitOrgScope` (`approval-service.ts:2755-2761`) is a strict equality; `businessUnitMemberScope` unchanged; pinned at `approval-service.test.ts:968-980` (an organization-less unit resolves to the dead literal) and the re-stamped `business-unit-member-org-screen.test.ts` fixtures. `teamIsProvablyOutsideOrg` keeps its no-organization limb (`:2584-2590`, cross-reference corrected) — outside the 7a-3 surface, as the report says.
- Seed loader: `loadExistingRecords` (`seed-loader.ts:3361-3384`) issues one scoped read; `decideWriteAction` loses `refuse`. **After certification a NULL holder goes unseen, it is not yet impossible**: the 18.x boot guard is marker-based (`organization-ownership-boot-guard.ts:37`, "boots, whatever the columns hold"), and the execution record itself cites 7b-3's measurement of a fresh birth-marked install writing NULL rows, with 7b-0 (NOT NULL at `createTable`) as the closure. Until then a scoped upsert over such a row inserts an organization-stamped twin beside it — the benign direction (no adoption, no cross-organization write, D9 stamps the twin). Residual R3.

**5. Wire change — the console needs no change.**
- objectui at the pinned sha `12dc7b4` (the objectui#12982 landing, regime C) and at `origin/main` (`cd4623d`): Setup lists declared rules from `GET /meta/sharing_rule`, not from `/sharing/rules`; it reads `GET /sharing/rules/:name` for one rule only, as `SharingRuleProjection { name, object_name, criteria, recipient_type, recipient_id, access_level }` (`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/sharing-rule-catalog.ts:73-80, 88-105`). `git grep` over `apps/*` and `packages/*` at `origin/main` finds zero `organization_id === null` / `== null` / `deploymentWide` readers. Nothing labels a declared rule by its NULL organization.
- In-repo consumers of the served row: `ruleReadsRowsOf` (`recipient-membership-recompute.ts:203`) reads `rule.organization_id == null` as "every row" — with the key absent on the deployment-wide projection the answer stays correct (the report's dedupe note). The four pins that read `organization_id: null` on the served shape (two dogfood files, `standalone-stack-seeder-declaration-copy.test.ts`) are rewritten to the marker and assert the key's absence.
- No published schema describes the served row beyond `SharingRuleRow` in `packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.ts:481-483` (`organization_id?: string | null`, no `deploymentWide`); no OpenAPI/zod response schema for `/sharing/rules` exists in `packages/spec` or `packages/server`. Residual R1.

**6. Tests — pins rewritten, none weakened; the ablation is well-formed.**
- Every replaced assertion is stronger or equal: `grantsAtRest` pins record AND organization of each grant where `sharedRecordIds` pinned ids; `getRule` → `null` by name and by id; `evaluateRule` → rejects `RULE_NOT_FOUND` with an empty grant table; the seed-loader pins add a `nullReads` spy on both the engine double and the real driver (`seed-loader-null-organization-holder.test.ts:122-130`, real-driver `:151-160`) and the `update` mode. The #7795 block is removed with its guard (the feature no longer exists; see R2 for the successor pin). One coverage note: the real-driver case "an unscoped load matches NULL rows and inserts no twin" was deleted rather than re-pinned; the behaviour is unchanged by this diff and the metadata-protocol twin keeps the unscoped case with an own row.
- Ablation: `:1780` (string organization) precedes `:1781`, so an unconditional `return SYSTEM_CTX` at `:1781` leaves org-stamped and declared cases untouched and reds exactly the two stored-organization-less cases (`:376`, `:459`) — the report's 2 red / 6 green. Restore verified by blob equality.

**7. Overlap with PR #24825 (7a-1) on `rule-criteria-org-scope.test.ts`** — #24825 is open, draft, head `2ee8e8d87`, base `main`, merge-base `307ce4c4b`. It rewrites the header (lines 29-80: "`applyTenantScope` turns `tenantId` into `organization_id = ?`"; `deal_p1` paragraphs) and the ORG-STAMPED case (`['deal_a1']`, matched 1). This PR rewrites the adjacent header paragraph (lines 44-62), adds `BootOptions`/`DECLARED`/`grantsAtRest` and four cases, and leaves the "`field = ? OR field IS NULL`" sentence (lines 51-55) in place. The second lander owes: (a) a textual merge of the two header rewrites into one that names neither a "platform-global sweep" (7a-1's wording, a class 7a-3 retires) nor an `OR IS NULL` arm (7a-3's remaining sentence, an arm 7a-1 retires); (b) 7a-1's ORG-STAMPED expectation kept, 7a-3's four cases kept; (c) the `driver.delete(OBJECT, 'deal_p1')` pre-step at `:362-363` and its comment become unnecessary once the arm is gone — drop or re-justify; (d) the report's "second interaction" note (RECORD_NOT_FOUND on the second walled projection over an organization-less record) is closed by 7a-1 and needs no carrier.

**8. Semver and Clause-② — correct.** AGENTS.md §3: `yes` takes at least `minor`; `(narrowing)` is BREAKING and must carry its FROM → TO and an ADR-0087 marker. The changeset has all three: `minor` x3, a bang in the subject, `FROM rule.organization_id === null TO rule.deploymentWide === true` with the two endpoints named, and `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. No `major` changeset exists anywhere in `.changeset/`; the step-7 siblings (`15212-8b-*`, `15212-webhook-declared-name-guard`) are `feat(...)!:` at `minor`, so this is the line's convention. The arm reading is right: `yes` because nothing an author declares or authors is refused (a declared rule keeps granting, the console's authoring door is untouched); `(narrowing)` because readers narrow — the new key on the wire is additive, but the removal of `organization_id` from the served declared row is the BREAKING half, and the changeset states it. The face is declaration (`Clause-②: yes`), hence `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ② Semver level

`minor` on `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, each with the BREAKING bang, the migration (the ceremony command, stated) and the ADR-0087 disposition — matches the repo rule and the line's precedent. Public surface added: `DeploymentWideSharingRule`, `isDeploymentWideSharingRule` (plugin-sharing exports, additive). Public surface removed: none exported (`assertCanDeletePlatformGlobalRule` was private); the `seed-loader` `refuse` decision was internal. The one wire shape change is the declared rule's served row.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **R1 (residual, spec lane, CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER when carried):** `SharingRuleRow` in `packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.ts:481` still declares `organization_id?: string | null` and no `deploymentWide`; the marker is a plugin-local type. Until the contract carries `deploymentWide?: true` (and says the key is absent under a wall), the served key is undocumented. Correctly outside this claim's file surface (⛔ spec is a published schema path); carrier: a step-7 follow-up on the spec lane.
- **R2 (residual, test pin):** the deleted #7795 block pinned "the refusal leaves the rule row AND every tenant's grants intact". Its successor on the new rule is unpinned: `deleteRule(orgLessRowId, ORG1_ADMIN)` and `deleteRule(orgLessName, ORG1_ADMIN)` should be pinned as a silent no-op that leaves the row and its grants in place (and a system context still deleting it). Today only `getRule`/`evaluateRule` on that row are pinned (`sharing-rule.test.ts:1101-1116, 1288-1292`); a regression to an unfiltered by-id lookup inside `deleteRule` would purge grants silently. Fix: about 12 lines in the `[#7761]` block.
- **R3 (residual, carried by 7b-0/7b-3):** the seed loader's NULL holder is unseen, not impossible, until the tenant column is NOT NULL at `createTable` (7b-0) and the auth-secret-less `os serve` composition refuses (7b-3). Consequence meanwhile: an organization-stamped twin beside a stray NULL row; no adoption, no cross-organization write.
- **R4 (residual, overlap):** the second of #24825 / #24828 to land owes the `rule-criteria-org-scope.test.ts` reconciliation in ① item 7.
- **Open question 1 of the report (A accepted):** `setDeclaredRuleScopes(ReadonlyArray of string or null)` and `resolveDeclaredRuleScopes` still spell `single` as `[null]` at the plugin door; translated at one line (`:538`), no NULL travels past it. Retyping both to the marker is about 10 lines and can ride the next step-7 part that touches `sharing-plugin.ts`. Related pre-existing observation: the service's constructor default is the `single` shape (`:512`, was `[null]`); the plugin sets scopes before any read (`sharing-plugin.ts:772-810`, only `registerService` between), so nothing is served before the posture is known.
- **Open question 2 (A accepted):** an engine that cannot answer reads as composing organizations — the refusing reading, and the same one `resolveSystemWriteOrganization` takes.
- **Open question 3 (A accepted):** `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` row 40 is a one-row citation drop forced by `check-system-context-census` after the guard's deletion; `content/docs/**` is not on the Prime Directive #14 register, and the Governed Surface Queue Guard is green. The `packages/runtime` and `packages/qa/dogfood` pin edits are consequences of the wire change and are inside the claim's "pins for the above".
- **Out-of-scope notes in the report** (`ruleReadsRowsOf` spelling, `teamIsProvablyOutsideOrg` NULL limb, stale `resolveSystemGrantOrganization` doc, `[tenant-audit]` warnings on the walled showcase boot): read and agreed as not this PR's; none is a leak on a certified database.
- **CI:** Test Core 1/6–6/6 were in progress at review time; the lane seat reads them green before queueing (AGENTS.md: `in_progress` is not a pass).

## Contract review (delta after PASS at 357025dc9)

Served-tier: CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER
Head-sha: 236d39daf47ce4b06c9e8757ccbe695af1ca1e19
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.ts + .changeset/24583-7a3-sharing-null-readers.md, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-rule-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-rule.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/rule-criteria-org-scope.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-plugin.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts (at 7c2eab929), packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts (main's hunk only), packages/client/src/index.ts, packages/spec/scripts/build-api-surface.ts, packages/spec/scripts/check-generated.ts, packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json, packages/spec/api-surface-signatures.json, packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json, packages/spec/scripts/build-spec-changes.ts, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, docs/adr/0131-total-organization-ownership-no-null-organization-id.md, AGENTS.md

Read-only delta review of PR #24828 at its new head, in a detached worktree, against the PASS record at `357025dc9`. Commits since the PASS: `228e74a00` (R1 + R2), `7d8257d60` (changeset), `32b3d1c54` (merge of `origin/main` through `7c2eab929`), `236d39daf` (R4). Merge-base moved `ddb3360a4` to `7c2eab929` = the 7a-1 landing (#24825).
